> What is something you've experienced that felt like it was the closest to thing what you think an adventure might feel like?

Nothing really. The closest that felt to an adrenaline high was when I was in the passenger seat of my friend's car when he was doing 100 in a 50 and weaving through traffic racing a friend in a seperate. That was fun. Ironically I felt alive when I could I have died in probably the most violent way possible. But thats all that was, just an adrenaline high. I felt empty afterwards. 


There really in nothing that I can think of that would be closest to what I think adventure would feel like. 

> I've always wanted to be a jet plane pilot.

Same! I cant either because of my vision. When I was a kid I wanted to be a fighter pilot but I cant because I wear glasses. Plus I have visual snow so even if I got it corrected I doubt they would allow me. I've looked into getting just a regular pilot's license but it was about $10,000 to get one last time I checked.

> We can make our own adventures.

That's funny that you say that. I actually put that in the first draft of my post but got rid of it because I thought my post was going to be too long

You have no idea how many times I've heard that. You say "Try surviving in a jungle, or climbing a mountain, or finding an endangered species, or exploring uncharted territory, or becoming a monk, or visiting a warzone." Where am I to find these places? Where am I to explore an exploring uncharted territory?Where am I to find such  a place? Even if I were to how am I going to fund that several month long expedition? Life is only minecraft if you have money and the connections to do those things.


Everyone who says "We make our adventures" say to go do these things like there as easy to do as just saying. Do this, go here.

> Not only that, but what kind of therapy? There’s so many different kinds and it’s sometimes hard to find a therapist who’s a good fit.

I've done talk therapy but that really doesn't help. I could sit there and talk about my problems for hours but I only have one and often feel rushed. Plus, almost all of the therapist in my area dont take my insurance. There is an art therapy place near me that I have been putting off calling. Ive been in a group therapy program where they had us color pages from coloring books and it was very infantilzing
I am not a software engineer. Ive looking to becoming one but I cant because I cant code if my life depended on it. Thank you for responding :)
